intent: Simplify how OverlappingFieldsCanBeMergedRule compares the arguments of two same-named fields: wrap all of a field's arguments in a synthetic ObjectValueNode, sort it, print it, and compare the strings, replacing the per-argument lookup. Validation results should not change (argument order ignored, any name/value difference still a conflict).

findings.title: Argument comparison now prints every field pair, ~28x slower for argument-less fields
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the cheap paths before printing: `const args1 = node1.arguments ?? []; const args2 = node2.arguments ?? []; if (args1.length !== args2.length) -> conflict; if (args1.length === 0) -> same;` and print only when both fields have arguments. Better still, memoize stringifyArguments per FieldNode (for example a Map<FieldNode, string> held next to cachedFieldsAndFragmentNames), so each node is sorted and printed once instead of once per pair.
findings.why_it_matters: Validating a document that repeats a field many times now costs much more CPU. findConflict runs for every pair of same-response-name fields (quadratic in the number of repeats), and this line now builds a synthetic ObjectValueNode, sorts it, and runs the visitor-based print() twice per pair, even when neither field has arguments. The removed sameArguments returned at once on a length mismatch and printed nothing for argument-less fields. Measured with the same script on base and head (babel-register, 3 runs averaged): 400 copies of `a` went from 15 ms to 429 ms; 1500 copies went from 148 ms to 6,273 ms; 400 copies of `b(x: 1, y: 2, z: 3)` went from 1,641 ms to 4,301 ms. A short unauthenticated query can now keep a server busy for seconds during validation. Restoring the length and empty fast paths, or printing each node once, removes the per-pair cost.
evidence: src/validation/rules/OverlappingFieldsCanBeMergedRule.ts:641-649 -- const inputObjectWithArgs: ObjectValueNode = { kind: Kind.OBJECT, fields: args.map(...) }; return print(sortValueNode(inputObjectWithArgs));
base (removed) -- if (arguments1.length !== arguments2.length) { return false; } return arguments1.every(...)  // no print for zero-arg fields

residual_risks: adversarial (local, anchor 50, P3): argument names that differ only in a digit run longer than ~15 digits (for example a99999999999999999 and a99999999999999998) compare equal under naturalCompare because of Number precision loss, so the stable sort keeps input order and reordered-but-identical arguments now report 'differing arguments'. The removed exact-name matching handled this; nested input objects already behaved this way since 40c160e9. A tie-break in sortValueNode's sortFields (naturalCompare(a, b) || (a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0)) would fix both cases. Real schemas almost never use such names.
Performance figures come from source run under @babel/register, not the built npm package. The absolute times will differ, but base and head ran under identical conditions.
testing_gaps: No test or benchmark guards the validation cost of many repeated overlapping fields (benchmark/ has no OverlappingFieldsCanBeMerged stress case). The 28x slowdown in finding #1 passes all 46 rule tests.

adversarial: duplicate argument names changed behavior and have no test. '{ f(a: 1, a: 1) f(a: 1, b: 2) }' produced no overlap conflict on base and does on head (UniqueArgumentNamesRule rejects such documents separately). A case in each order would lock in the new symmetric behavior.
